## Spatial & Geometric Definition
* Geometry Type: Point (Feature_Stationing_Point).

* Spatial Delineation: Regular linear control points established along the alignment of an embankment centerline, access roadway, channel cut, or stone dike.

* Format: Standard civil engineering linear stationing markers (0+00, 1+00, 5+00, etc.), where each station represents 100.0 linear feet.

### Primary Engineering & Operational Objectives
* Linear Coordinate Referencing: Establishes the authoritative linear measurement system used across all contract plan sheets, cross-sections, and inspection reports.

* Asset Tracking & Work Measurement: Links geotechnical borings, culverts, spillway notches, and riprap armor transitions to an unambiguous linear coordinate along the structure.

* Construction Progress Verification: Enables contract field inspectors to precisely verify contractor pay-application quantities based on physical station intervals.

### Typical Specifications & Geometric Properties
* Station Intervals: Points established every 100 ft on tangents and every 50 ft or 25 ft on horizontal curves.

* Attribute Domains: Alignment Name, Station Number (XX+YY), Design Crest Grade, Left/Right Slope Offsets, and Elevation.

### Survey & Layout Implementation
* Staking Standards: Survey field crews install marked wooden hubs, iron pins, or aluminum caps during construction, tied to the project horizontal baseline.

### Quality Control, Inspection & Long-Term Maintenance
* Permanent Reference Hubs: Key stationing monuments (every 1,000 ft) cast into concrete markers or stamped brass disks to serve as permanent physical recovery points for post-flood inspection teams.

## Spatial Feature Attributes
### Definition
Feature Stationing: This refers to a system of linear referencing used to locate features along an alignment, such as an embankment or road. It is used for design, construction, and maintenance purposes. Reference points, generally expressed in linear units (typically feet), that allow identification of specific locations on engineered structures such as levees, control structures, roads, or walls.

### Purpose
Feature stationing is used to tie design documents, construction records, inspections, and maintenance activities to precise locations along an engineered structure. By assigning station codes and associated elevations, project teams can consistently reference, locate, and document conditions, work items, or features along the structure.

### Applicability
Feature stationing is applicable to any linear engineered feature within Upper Mississippi River System (UMRS) restoration projects where precise, repeatable location referencing is needed. Common examples include levees, floodwalls, spillways, roads, channels, and other structures where plans and profiles are based on stationing. (UMRR Design Handbook, 2012)

### Notes
Restoration features now have a Program_UID field to distinguish between NESP and UMRR features. Aliases without program identification will be created for any field that currently has UMRR in the name, so they can be used for NESP or UMRR data.

Attribute criteria for each field includes the following:

* Attribute Status – defines whether the field requires a value or if it is optional based on available information.
* Phases – indicates the earliest time in the project lifecycle values for this attribute are available.
* Digitizing requirements – indicates when the field value should be entered in the attribute table.

Geometry Note: No Z values are needed for this feature.

## FeatureStationing
(point) – Reference points, generally in feet, that allow identification of specific locations on engineered structures.

## Parameters

### Program_UID
Designate program NESP or UMRR.

### Project_ID (alias: PROJECT_ID)
Foreign key to the unique NESP/UMRR project ID.

### Type (alias: Restoration_Type)
A broad classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into categories of similar function.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Restoration_Type</td>
      <td>Support feature</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### SubType (alias: Subtype)
A classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into specific design feature categories.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Feature Stationing</td>
      <td>Stationing reference points on engineered features.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### RestorFeatStatus
A description of the status of the individual restoration. It also includes the party responsible for the individual feature.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Planned</td>
      <td>Feature is in a USACE planning stage.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by USACE. If a feature has been planned and built by USACE, once constructed, it will always be considered USACE built even if it has been repaired under later project stages.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature that was not built by USACE has been enhanced by a feature that was USACE built or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that was not built by USACE has been directly improved or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Planned</td>
      <td>A feature that is planned by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by another organization or government agency and is an integral part of the UMRR project.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature, that was built by another organization or government agency, has been enhanced by a feature that was built or repaired by a non-USACE organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that has been directly improved or repaired by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### sdsFeatureName
The common name of the feature.

### sdsFeatureDescription
A narrative describing the feature.

### RestorFeatVdatum
Vertical datum of elevations recorded in the attribute table or used as feature z values.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>MSL 1912</td>
      <td>Mean Sea Level of 1912</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>NGVD 1929</td>
      <td>National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>NAVD 1988</td>
      <td>North American Vertical Datum of 1988</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other</td>
      <td>Other, note datum in sdsFeatureDescription</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Unknown</td>
      <td>Unknown vertical datum</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### StationCode
Linear reference identifier for the station point, typically recorded in engineering station format (e.g., 10+00), representing distance along a baseline or alignment.

### StationElevation
Elevation at the station point, referenced to the specified vertical datum in RestorFeatVdatum.

### sdsMetaDataID
References attached metadata.

### RestorFeatIDPK
Primary key used to uniquely identify the restoration feature record.

### sdsID
Identifier used to link the feature to supporting SDS (spatial data system) records or related datasets.

### mediaIDFK
Foreign key used to reference associated media (e.g., photographs, drawings, as-built plans) documenting the station location.
